This is TyFi:
parametric typhoon insurance for Filipino farmers,
built on Stellar.
In the next four minutes,
we run the whole pipeline live on testnet.
A farmer signs in with a passkey,
with no seed phrase.
The farming co-op governs the insurance vault
through a DAO.
When a typhoon hits,
an oracle proves the storm crossed a
payout threshold with a zero-knowledge proof,
the vault verifies that proof on-chain,
and the payout lands in the farmer's wallet.
We start with the wallet.
On the passkey page,
the farmer names the wallet and taps create.
The device creates a passkey,
and our factory contract deploys a smart
wallet bound to it.
There is no seed phrase,
and no private key in the browser.
From here on,
every transaction is approved with the same
fingerprint or face,
and checked on-chain by the wallet's own __check_auth.
Here is the deployment on Stellar Expert.
The co-op funds the wallet and verifies
the farm through the vault's admin multisig.
The farmer then joins the reinsurance pool
as a liquidity provider,
and insures a rice farm in Eastern Visayas.
Each of those steps is signed with
the passkey and settled on testnet.
Now, governance.
In the DAO tab,
the farmer's voting power is read straight
from their liquidity shares in the vault.
A new proposal is open,
and the farmer votes for it.
The passkey signs the vote,
and the tally updates on-chain.
Quorum is 30% of all shares,
and premium changes need a 60% supermajority.
Earlier, the co-op passed proposal 6:
raise the Eastern Visayas premium multiplier to 125%.
It then sat in a 12-hour timelock,
so members could react before anything changed.
The timelock is over.
The co-op made this farmer a DAO
executor, so the farmer taps finalize,
and signs with the passkey.
The DAO contract then calls the vault
contract directly.
The vault only accepts parameter changes from
its DAO.
In the invocation tree,
you can see the DAO calling update_premium_rate
on the vault,
and the Eastern Visayas multiplier moving from 100 to 125.
Then the storm.
Typhoon Odette crosses Eastern Visayas,
and the oracle reads 172 km/h.
That number stays private.
The oracle signs the reading,
and generates a Groth16 proof that its
registered key signed a reading at or
above the 150 km/h band.
The vault rebuilds every public input itself:
the oracle's key,
the typhoon, the region,
the band, and the damage.
It checks the proof with Soroban's BN254
pairing functions, in about 30M instructions,
and stores only the band.
With consensus recorded,
the farmer claims,
and the vault pays 85% of the
coverage straight to the passkey wallet.
Forged proofs fail.
Change the damage,
the region, the wind band,
or the oracle key,
and the pairing check rejects it.
The contract test suite covers each case.
The same statement is also written in
Noir, and one oracle signature satisfies both circuits.
And admin calls now require the multisig,
closing a zero-threshold bypass we found this week.
Every step has a testnet transaction you
can open on Stellar Expert.
The contracts, the app,
the oracle and both circuits are open
source under the MIT license,
with a replication guide to run all
of it yourself.
That's TyFi.
